name: std-thread
description: std-thread — forum-style nested replies with collapse. Owns ThreadPost (persistent). INIT fetches, scoped by @config.threadRootId when set (blank = every root, the default). The list holds top-level posts, each with its replies nested (one level). REPLY persists a child post under @payload.parentId in the same thread root, stamped with the real @user identity, and adds it to the parent's replies and replyCount. A consumer that mounts this as page comments forwards its own document-opened signal to SET_THREAD_ROOT { rootId }, which stamps @entity.replyRootId (scratch — the persisted threadRootId column is written only by the reply persist create) and refetches filtered by the payload; a plain INIT re-entry now also falls back through @entity.replyRootId before @config.threadRootId, so it stays scoped to the last SET_THREAD_ROOT instead of re-widening — only the after-create/after-select refetches still scope directly off their own event payload. Layer 3 variants override `bodyContent` to deliver chat-bubble, email-threaded, or linear-comments UX while inheriting the same trait, state machine, emits, and listens. A non-empty sectionTitle switches the default bodyContent into titled-comments mode: header + post list + a standalone composer button (without it an empty thread has no REPLY emitter at all — the affordance only existed per-row).

bodyContent.description: Render-ui SExpr rendered after thread posts load. Default is the canonical forum-style data-list. Layer 3 variants override this with their own tree (chat bubbles, email-threaded cards, linear comment stacks, etc.) to deliver entirely different thread UX while inheriting the same trait, state machine, emits, and listens.

replyRoles.label: Roles that can reply

sectionTitle.description: Section header rendered by the default bodyContent when non-empty, along with a standalone composer button — the only REPLY affordance an empty thread has. Blank (the default) keeps the bare post list for embedded threads that bring their own chrome (chat rails, custom comment sections).

viewerRole.description: The signed-in viewer's role that each action's `roles` is checked against. Bind it explicitly at the call site (e.g. `viewerRole: @user.role`) in an app whose identity carries a role; left empty, only actions with no `roles` show.
